snippet.title: Jeffrey Epstein was killed, says forensic scientist who studied his post mortem files
snippet.description:
Professor Michael Freeman, a forensic scientist who spent a year examining Jeffrey Epstein's post-mortem files, believes he was killed.

Epstein was found dead in his prison cell in August 2019. His death was ruled as suicide.

Sky News did not receive a response from the Federal Bureau of Prisons. The Office of Chief Medical Examiner continues to stand by its determination of suicide. 

Anyone feeling emotionally distressed or suicidal can call Samaritans for help on 116 123 or email jo@samaritans.org in the UK.

Alternatively, you can call Mind's support line on 0300 102 1234, or NHS on 111.

snippet.title: Carney Just Went Around Trump to Reach Half the World
snippet.description:
Donald Trump spent the year trying to box Canada in with tariffs. Mark Carney answered with four international summits in eight days, from Dublin and Manila to Phnom Penh and Shenzhen, where Trump and Xi Jinping are both expected.

Christine Nakamura of the Asia Pacific Foundation of Canada explains why Asia is central to Carney's plan to double Canada's exports beyond the United States, what the new Philippines and ASEAN agreements mean for Canadian businesses, and why a young, fast growing middle class could be Canada's next generation of customers.

snippet.title: Steph Curry's CRAZIEST Shot Wasn't In The NBA… 😭🏀
snippet.description:
What's harder: hitting a 75-footer or hitting a hole in one? On Hot Ones, Sean Evans asked Steph Curry if making a hole in one feels like draining a shot from 75 feet on the court, and Curry's answer was surprising. When he lets a 75-footer fly, he's probably made it before in practice or in a game, so honestly he expects it to go in. A hole in one is different: even if you stripe it right at the flag, the odds of it actually dropping are slim to none. So when he was asked on TV what feels better, a buzzer beater or a hole in one, he didn't hesitate. The hole in one. That's because of July 15, 2023 at the American Century Championship in Lake Tahoe, when the then 35-year-old Golden State Warriors superstar stepped up to the 152-yard par-3 7th hole at Edgewood Tahoe. His tee shot landed a couple feet from the pin, took one bounce and disappeared into the cup. It was the first hole in one ever on that hole, only the fifth ace in tournament history, and just the second of Curry's life. He spiked his hat, threw a finger in the air and sprinted all the way down the fairway to slap the flagstick, while LeBron James and Patrick Mahomes lost it online. The next day, Curry won the whole tournament with a walk-off eagle putt on 18. Is a hole in one really better than a game-winning buzzer beater?
